about.title: Rohnert Park Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product can turn an ordinary day in Rohnert Park into a trip to Sonoma County's emergency rooms — whether it's a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a tool that shatters on the job, or a car part that fails on Rohnert Park Expressway. California's strict liability framework matters here because it shifts the focus away from proving a manufacturer was careless and onto whether the product itself was flawed in its design, its assembly, or the warnings that came with it. That distinction can make a real difference for someone recovering from an injury while also trying to keep up with medical bills. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly — we simply connect Rohnert Park residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, help preserve the product as evidence, and explain what a claim might involve. There's no cost to get connected, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Rohnert Park Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove a manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused harm. That can streamline what you need to show.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product, which broadens who may be accountable for your injury.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An attorney can advise you early on to keep the product itself intact and unaltered, since it's often the most important piece of evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew the product was defective?
items.answer: No — California's strict liability standard generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. This applies to design flaws, manufacturing errors, and inadequate warnings alike. An attorney can help sort out which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near Rohnert Park Expressway or Redwood Drive — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily for a product defect claim, but if the incident happened during a vehicle-related failure along a busy corridor like Rohnert Park Expressway, there may be overlapping factors worth examining, such as auto parts versus road conditions. An independent attorney can help determine which laws and parties are relevant to your specific injury.

items.question: What should I do with the product that caused my injury?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, if at all possible — don't repair, discard, or alter it. The product is often central evidence in these claims. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on proper preservation.
